terra.problem: The return-address joke makes the Father and the Son the subject of the humor.
The hypothetical about a father hearing news is a scenario about a parent.
It says the news made the elder write the way he does. The text says he was overjoyed, but does not give that reason for his writing.
The statement that the Sabbath is a commandment is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The elder says what 'we have worked for.' Calling it 'their work' specifies whose work it is beyond what the text says.
The elder says what 'we have worked for,' not specifically what 'they've worked for.'
The statement that nobody gets only one goes beyond the verse's statement that whoever remains in Christ's teaching has both.
The elder says he hopes to come, not that he plans to show up.
